questions.topic: Introduction to Fabrication and Welding Practice
questions.stem: Joining two pieces of metal by heating them until they melt and fuse together is
questions.explanation: Welding fuses the parent metals, usually with filler metal.

questions.topic: Safety Precautions in Welding and Fabrication Workshop
questions.stem: Fumes given off when welding galvanised steel are dangerous mainly because they contain
options: pure oxygen from the burning coating
questions.explanation: Burning off the zinc coating releases zinc oxide fumes that cause flu-like metal fume fever.

questions.stem: In a fabrication workshop, gas cylinders should be kept
options: chained upright in a ventilated store
in the welding booth for convenience
questions.explanation: Cylinders need secure, ventilated storage away from heat, sparks and arcs.

questions.stem: On a welding symbol, a triangle drawn BELOW the reference line indicates a
options: fillet weld on the other side
fillet weld on the arrow side
questions.explanation: Symbols below the reference line refer to the arrow side (ISO/AWS convention); the triangle denotes a fillet weld.

questions.stem: A welder gets a metal splinter in the eye. The first aider should
options: rub the eye hard until the splinter comes out
remove the splinter with a pin
flush with clean water, get help
ignore it until the next day
questions.explanation: Rubbing or probing can cause further injury; flush and get medical attention.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a NON-FERROUS metal?
questions.explanation: Copper contains no iron.

questions.stem: The ability of a metal to absorb energy and resist breaking under shock loads is
questions.explanation: Toughness is resistance to fracture under impact.

questions.stem: Galvanised sheet used to make buckets and water tanks is mild steel coated with
questions.explanation: Galvanising applies a zinc coating to protect steel from rust.

questions.topic: Selection of Suitable Metals for Specific Jobs
questions.stem: Which metal is MOST suitable for the cutting edge of a cold chisel?
questions.explanation: High-carbon steel can be hardened and tempered to hold an edge.

questions.stem: A hardened punch is tempered to a purple-brown colour in order to
options: make it as soft as possible for easy filing
questions.explanation: Tempering trades a little hardness for toughness; oxide colours indicate the temperature.

questions.stem: The tool used to cut thin sheet metal along straight and gentle curved lines by hand is the
questions.explanation: Snips cut thin sheet by shearing.

questions.topic: Equipment Set-up for Gas and Arc Welding and Fabrication
questions.stem: Before connecting an arc welding machine, the welder should check that
options: the electrodes are wet so that they will not overheat
the helmet lens is clear glass
cables and earth clamp are sound
the floor is wet to cool the work
questions.explanation: Damaged cables and poor earthing cause shocks and unstable arcs.

questions.stem: Work is held firmly on a bench for filing and sawing in the
questions.explanation: The bench vice grips work for bench operations.

questions.topic: Measuring Instruments, Marking Out and Cutting Tools
questions.stem: The measuring instrument used to check the thickness of a sheet to 0.01 mm is the
questions.explanation: A micrometer measures to 0.01 mm.

questions.topic: Parts and Accessories for Gas and Arc Welding
questions.stem: In oxy-acetylene equipment, the device that stops a flame travelling back into the hose and cylinder is the
questions.explanation: Flashback arrestors quench reversed flames and stop reverse gas flow.

questions.stem: Partly blocked torch nozzles should be cleaned with
options: a drill bit that enlarges the hole
questions.explanation: Tip cleaners remove deposits without enlarging or damaging the orifice.

questions.topic: Preparation of Acetylene Gas from Carbide
questions.stem: When water drips on calcium carbide in a generator, the by-product left behind is
questions.explanation: CaC2 + 2H2O → C2H2 + Ca(OH)2; the residue is slaked lime.

questions.stem: Using a rule of about 40 A for each millimetre of core diameter, the suitable current for a 3.2 mm electrode is about
questions.explanation: 40 x 3.2 = 128 A (manufacturers give a range around this).

questions.stem: Low-hydrogen electrodes that have absorbed moisture should be
questions.explanation: Moisture adds hydrogen to the weld, causing cracking and porosity; baking removes it.

questions.topic: Equipment for Fault Detection and Trouble Shooting
questions.stem: A magnetic particle test can detect surface cracks in
questions.explanation: Magnetic particle inspection works only on ferromagnetic materials.

questions.stem: An arc welder sets 25 V and 120 A. The electrical power in the arc is
In oxy-acetylene welding the heat comes from
options: burning a fuel gas with oxygen
questions.explanation: Gas welding uses the flame from combustion of acetylene in oxygen.

questions.stem: Which step comes FIRST in a typical fabrication job?
options: Studying the drawing and marking out
questions.explanation: Work begins with interpreting the drawing and marking out the material.

questions.stem: Two plates overlapping each other and welded along the edges form a
questions.explanation: In a lap joint one plate overlaps the other.

questions.stem: Marking out a shape by drawing lines directly on the metal using scriber, rule and square is
questions.explanation: Direct marking uses measuring and marking tools on the job itself.

questions.stem: Templates are especially useful when
options: many identical parts are to be marked
questions.explanation: A template allows the same shape to be marked quickly and accurately many times.

questions.stem: In leftward gas welding, the blowpipe flame points
options: ahead of the weld towards the unwelded joint
questions.explanation: In leftward welding the flame points forward, preheating the joint; it suits thin plate.

questions.stem: A steel band is to wrap once round a drum of 560 mm diameter with a 20 mm overlap. The length of strip needed is about
Which of these is a PERMANENT fastening method?
questions.explanation: Rivets are removed only by destroying them.

questions.topic: Rivets, Bolts and Nuts, and Screws
questions.stem: For an 8 mm rivet, using pitch = 3d and edge distance = 1.5d, the pitch and edge distance are
questions.explanation: Pitch = 3 x 8 = 24 mm; edge distance = 1.5 x 8 = 12 mm.

questions.topic: Rivets, Bolts and Nuts, and Screws
questions.stem: A rivet with a countersunk head is used where
options: the joint must be taken apart often
the plates are made of wood
questions.explanation: Countersunk rivets sit flush with the surface.

questions.stem: The forging tool with grooved faces, used in pairs to round off a bar, is the
questions.explanation: Swages form round or shaped sections.

questions.stem: Reducing the thickness of a bar and increasing its length by hammering is
questions.explanation: Drawing down lengthens and thins the bar.

questions.topic: Preparation of Welding Surfaces and Edges
questions.stem: Before welding, the oil film on a plate is best removed by
options: painting it with red oxide primer
heating it until it smokes and then welding
questions.explanation: Degreasing removes oil that would cause porosity.

questions.stem: Weld metal that flows over the plate surface without fusing to it is
questions.explanation: Overlap (cold lap) is unfused metal lying on the parent plate, often from slow travel or low current.

questions.stem: A fire starts near a welding bay in Kano. On investigation, which condition is MOST likely to have caused it?
options: Oily rags left near the bench
questions.explanation: Oily rags are flammable and can be ignited by sparks.

questions.topic: Surface Furnishing for Fabrication and Welding
questions.stem: Spraying molten zinc or aluminium onto a steel surface to protect it is
questions.explanation: Metal spraying deposits molten metal droplets as a protective coat.

questions.stem: An open tray with a base 200 mm x 150 mm and sides 40 mm high is made from one sheet by folding up the sides. The size of the blank needed (ignoring bend allowance) is
questions.explanation: Add a 40 mm side on each side: 200 + 80 = 280 mm; 150 + 80 = 230 mm.

questions.stem: A person who works in a welding shop for wages paid by the owner is an
questions.explanation: An employee works for an employer in return for pay.

questions.topic: Factors for Setting up a Workshop
questions.stem: A welder buys 5 kg of electrodes at ₦2,800 per kg and 2 sheets at ₦18,500 each for a job. The cost of these materials is

(a) Explain the following heat treatment processes: (i) hardening, (ii) annealing, (iii) normalising, (iv) case-hardening. [8 marks]
(b) Describe how a cold chisel is hardened and tempered in the workshop. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) hardening: heat above upper critical temperature, quench in water/oil
2 marks: (a)(ii) annealing: heat above critical, cool very slowly in furnace/ashes to soften
2 marks: (a)(iii) normalising: heat above critical, cool in still air to refine grain
2 marks: (a)(iv) case-hardening: add carbon to surface of low-carbon steel (carburise), then quench to harden surface
2 marks: (b) heat cutting end to cherry red (above critical)
1 mark: (b) quench the end in water
2 marks: (b) polish the end to see oxide colours; residual heat from shank runs colours to tip
2 marks: (b) when purple/brown reaches the edge, quench fully
questions.explanation: Hardening quenches from above critical; annealing cools slowly; normalising cools in air; case-hardening carburises then quenches. Chisel: heat to cherry red, quench end, polish, let colours run, quench at purple-brown.

questions.stem:
(a) State four functions of the flux coating on an arc welding electrode. [4 marks]
(b) Explain how an electrode is selected for a job. [5 marks]
(c) Compare a.c. and d.c. arc welding machines under three headings. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: produces shielding gas, forms slag to protect weld, stabilises arc, adds alloying elements, deoxidises weld metal (1 each)
5 marks: (b) consider: type of parent metal, thickness of plate, welding position, type of current/polarity, required strength/electrode classification (1 each)
2 marks: (c) cost: a.c. transformer cheaper than d.c. rectifier/generator
2 marks: (c) arc stability: d.c. more stable, better for thin and positional work
2 marks: (c) arc blow/polarity: a.c. less arc blow; d.c. allows choice of polarity
questions.explanation: Flux shields, forms slag, stabilises the arc, alloys and deoxidises. Select by metal, thickness, position, current and classification. A.C. sets are cheap with less arc blow; d.c. gives steadier arcs and polarity choice.

questions.stem:
(a) Name and describe four types of welded joint. [8 marks]
(b) Explain why edges of thick plates are bevelled before butt welding. [3 marks]
(c) Sketch-describe a double-V butt preparation and state one advantage over a single-V. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) butt joint: plates edge to edge in same plane
2 marks: (a) lap joint: plates overlapping
2 marks: (a) tee joint: one plate at right angles to the other forming a T
2 marks: (a) corner joint: plates meeting at their edges at an angle forming a corner (or edge joint)
3 marks: (b) to allow full penetration through the thickness and access for the electrode/flame
2 marks: (c) both sides bevelled to form two Vs meeting at a root face in the middle
2 marks: (c) advantage: less weld metal and less distortion than single-V (balanced welding)
questions.explanation: Butt, lap, tee, corner joints. Bevelling gives full penetration. Double-V uses less metal and balances distortion.

questions.topic: Rivets, Bolts and Nuts, and Screws
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between permanent and temporary fasteners, giving two examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the steps in making a riveted lap joint with snap-head rivets. [6 marks]
(c) Two 4 mm plates are joined with 5 mm rivets. Using a head allowance of 1.5d, calculate the rivet length. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) permanent: cannot be removed without damage
1 mark: (a) examples: rivets, welding, soldering (any two)
2 marks: (a) temporary: can be removed and reused
1 mark: (a) examples: bolts and nuts, screws, cotter pins (any two)
1 mark: (b) mark out and drill holes in both plates in line
1 mark: (b) deburr and insert rivet
1 mark: (b) support head in dolly/snap
1 mark: (b) draw plates together with set
1 mark: (b) hammer shank to swell and rough-shape
1 mark: (b) finish head with snap
1 mark: (c) grip = 4 + 4 = 8 mm
2 marks: (c) length = 8 + 1.5 x 5 = 15.5 mm
questions.explanation: Permanent: rivets, welds; temporary: bolts, screws. Riveting: drill, insert, support, draw up, swell, snap. Length = 8 + 7.5 = 15.5 mm.

questions.topic: Surface Furnishing for Fabrication and Welding
questions.stem:
(a) State four reasons for finishing fabricated work. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the following surface finishing methods: (i) painting, (ii) galvanising, (iii) oiling. [6 marks]
(c) Describe the steps in preparing a steel gate for painting. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: prevent rust/corrosion, improve appearance, identification, increase life, hygiene (1 each)
2 marks: (b)(i) painting: applying primer and finishing coats by brush or spray
2 marks: (b)(ii) galvanising: dipping cleaned steel in molten zinc
2 marks: (b)(iii) oiling: applying thin oil film to bright metal to prevent rust temporarily
5 marks: (c) remove slag and spatter; grind welds; remove rust with wire brush/emery; degrease; apply primer before final coats (1 each)
questions.explanation: Finishing protects and beautifies. Painting uses primer and topcoats; galvanising dips in zinc; oiling gives a temporary film. Prepare by removing slag, grinding, de-rusting, degreasing and priming.

questions.topic: Factors for Setting up a Workshop
questions.stem:
(a) Define entrepreneurship. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between small-scale and large-scale enterprises under three headings. [6 marks]
(c) State seven factors to consider in setting up a welding workshop. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the process of identifying opportunities, starting and managing a business while bearing risks for profit
2 marks: (b) capital: small-scale little capital vs large-scale huge capital
2 marks: (b) workforce: few vs many employees
2 marks: (b) management/output: owner-managed and small output vs professional management and mass output
7 marks: (c) any seven: cost/capital, site, weather, availability of materials, manpower, market, source of power, transportation, security (1 each)
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is starting and running a business at risk. Small firms have little capital, few staff and owner management. Factors: cost, site, weather, materials, manpower, market, power, transport.
